One professional foundation, applied across the energy lifecycle.
Energy programmes carry connected risks. Reporting often does not.

Energy and utilities programmes become harder to control when technical scope, regulatory gates, outage windows, contractor interfaces, cost forecasts, risk, change and operational readiness are managed as separate conversations. The result is late intervention, reactive reporting and reduced confidence when leaders must make high-consequence decisions.
The purpose of project controls is not to produce more dashboards. It is to make safer, earlier and better-informed intervention possible.
Engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning are not governed as one integrated promise.
Supply-chain, regulatory, safety and interface risks surface after recovery options have narrowed.
Project data is reported without connecting delivery decisions to reliability, readiness or benefits.
Four pathways for different levels of energy responsibility.

Each route is designed around the decisions professionals make across energy projects, programmes, portfolios and PMOs. The six-credit pathways combine mandatory core learning with specialist choices; PMO Certified is a focused four-credit route.

Build a project-management foundation for the energy sector.

Explore the Associate Project Management Pathway: a focused three-credit route combining PMP development (2 credits) with the AI in Project Controls Certificate (1 credit). Commercial instalments may be available for up to 24 months; funded and bursary terms are assessed separately.
The final pathway, module mix, access route, fees and professional outcomes are confirmed through a written KBC assessment.
What is the difference between the Funded Route and IPC Bursary Route?

The Funded Route is supported through the Department for Education and is subject to employment, residency, employer, prior-learning and funding requirements. The IPC Bursary Route is an alternative contribution towards selected pathway fees where DfE funding is unavailable or unsuitable.
Is the DfE Funded Route guaranteed?

No. It is potentially fully funded for eligible six-credit pathways, but funding is subject to the applicable rules, employer participation, available funding, prior-learning assessment and written confirmation.
Is this pathway only for renewable energy professionals?

No. The sector page is designed for professionals across power generation, electricity networks, renewables, oil and gas, decommissioning, nuclear, water, utilities, storage and energy-transition programmes, subject to role and pathway fit.
Can I tailor my Operational or Strategic pathway?

The pathway builder shows the intended structure: PMP and AI are core, with specialist choices. The final combination must be approved against role responsibilities, employer priorities, evidence opportunities and funding requirements.
Is the AI in Project Controls Certificate mandatory?
It is positioned as a mandatory core component of the six-credit Operational, Strategic and Chartered pathways in this page structure.
Does the Chartered Pathway guarantee ChPP status?

No. It supports senior evidence and chartered-readiness development. ChPP and any other professional recognition are awarded only by the relevant professional organisation after its full requirements are met.
How does the PMO Certified route differ?

PMO Certified is a focused four-credit route built around Certified PMO Professional Level 6. Its funding and IPC bursary terms are confirmed separately because it does not use the same six-credit structure.

It means eligible applications are assessed in the order they are completed, subject to pathway suitability, employer or bursary approval and available places. It does not override the eligibility or approval process.
What if my employer cannot support the required paid learning time?
The DfE route may not be suitable. The IPC Bursary Route may provide an alternative professional-development option with flexible instalments, subject to approval and availability.
What is the best next step?
Use the quick eligibility check, then book a one-to-one information session to review your current role, pathway fit, funding or bursary route and the evidence you can create at work.
